question: What are Alphabet, Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft each currently guiding for capital expenditures, and how do they line up on a calendar-2026 basis?
grading: Reference-free recency: use each company’s latest guide before the run timestamp, date it and preserve its calendar/fiscal and lease definitions. At the October 1 snapshot, CY2026: Alphabet $195–205B; Meta $130–145B including finance-lease principal; Amazon ~$220B cash capex; Microsoft ~$175B including finance leases/excluding operating leases. Do not treat Microsoft’s fiscal FY2027 or Q1 figures as calendar totals, or invent a harmonized cash basis.
answer: As of October 1, 2026, all four provide calendar-2026 capex numbers: Alphabet USD 195–205 billion (July 22 Q2 call); [G28-E1] Meta USD 130–145 billion including finance-lease principal payments (July 29 Q2 release); [G28-E2] Amazon approximately USD 220 billion in cash capex (July 30 Q2 call); [G28-E3] Microsoft approximately USD 175 billion (July 29 FY2026 Q4 call), including finance leases but excluding operating leases. Microsoft lowered the displayed capex amount because extending building useful lives shifts some future leases to operating classification; investment expectations apart from that change were unchanged. [G28-E4] Nominal ordering is Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, but the lease definitions differ, so these are not fully harmonized cash-spending measures. Microsoft separately expects FY2027 capex to grow YoY and Q1 FY2027 capex above USD 50 billion; those fiscal guides are not additional CY2026 totals. [G28-E4]

output.answer:
Here's how the four hyperscalers' latest capex guidance stacks up. All four figure below are already their **calendar-2026** guidance (Alphabet, Meta, and Amazon are calendar-year reporters; Microsoft guides explicitly on a calendar-year basis).

## Current guidance

**Alphabet — $195B–$205B (CY2026)**
Raised a second time on the Q2 2026 call (July 22, 2026) from a prior $180B–$190B, citing "an acceleration in the delivery of capacity to meet growing demand." Q2 capex alone was $44.9B, which pushed free cash flow negative (−$5.9B). Management flagged further significant increases in 2027. ([Trefis](https://www.trefis.com/stock/googl/articles/616790/how-has-alphabet-stocks-story-changed/2026-09-28), [TIKR](https://www.tikr.com/blog/alphabets-free-cash-flow-just-went-negative-heres-what-the-debt-behind-it-says))

**Amazon — ~$220B (CY2026, "cash capex")**
Initially guided $180B–$190B, lifted to ~$200B, then to ~$220B on the August 2026 call. Andy Jassy attributed the extra $20B to higher memory-chip costs rather than a change in the underlying build plan, and said Amazon still won't have enough capacity to meet 2026 demand. ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/amazon-raised-2026-capex-guide-114017457.html), [Leverage Shares](https://leverageshares.com/en-eu/insights/amazon-q2-2026-earnings-shows-aws-growth-accelerates))

**Microsoft — ~$175B (CY2026)**
This is the one that moved *down*: from ~$190B in April 2026 to ~$175B in July. Importantly, the cut was not a spending reduction — it stemmed from extending the assumed useful life of data-center/office properties from 15 to 25 years, which reclassifies more future leases from finance to operating leases (and finance leases are counted in capex, operating leases are not). Microsoft says underlying investment expectations are unchanged. Q4 FY2026 capex was $41B; Q1 FY2027 is guided >$50B; FY2026 actual came in at $115.9B. ([Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/analysis/microsofts-175-billion-capex-bet-raises-the-stakes-for-azure-growth-200688792), [Fortune transcript](https://fortune.com/company/microsoft/earnings/q4-2026))

**Meta — $130B–$145B (CY2026)**
Walked up through the year: $115B–$135B → $125B–$145B → $130B–$145B (narrowed at Q2 on July 29, 2026). The figure **includes principal payments on finance leases**. Q2 capex was $31.1B; free cash flow collapsed to $784M from $8.55B a year earlier. ([Yahoo/24-7 Wall St](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/meta-become-mega-cloud-operator-154422140.html), [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/09/24/meta-145-billion-capex-military-budgets))

## Calendar-2026 lineup

| Company | CY2026 guidance | Midpoint |
|---|---|---|
| Amazon | ~$220B | $220B |
| Alphabet | $195B–$205B | $200B |
| Microsoft | ~$175B | $175B |
| Meta | $130B–$145B | ~$137.5B |
| **Total** | | **~$732B** |

That's roughly a 75–80% jump over the prior year's combined total (~$410B). For reference, third-party tallies of the four have recently clustered around **$740B–$760B**.

## Two important caveats on comparability

1. **Definitions differ.** Microsoft's and Meta's figures **include finance-lease principal**; Amazon's ~$220B is explicitly *cash capex* and excludes finance leases (so Amazon's total spend on an all-in basis is higher than the headline). Alphabet reports capex gross of finance leases but doesn't lead with the same framing. So the numbers aren't perfectly apples-to-apples.

2. **Timing/fiscal mismatch.** Microsoft's FY2026 ended June 30, 2026, and its FY2027 straddles CY2026 and CY2027. The ~$175B is management's own calendar-year framing, not a fiscal-year figure — be careful not to mix it with the $115.9B FY2026 actual or the ~$180B+ FY2027 expectations.

One other pattern worth noting: three of the four raised guidance during 2026 (Alphabet, Amazon, Meta), while Microsoft's headline declined purely for accounting reasons. If you're tracking the trajectory into 2027, Alphabet and Meta have both signaled further meaningful increases, and Amazon analysts see cumulative 2026–2028 spend around $827B.
